expectations.text: [control:no-stream-trap-failure] The stream consumer gets past the invalid frame and reaches the end of the replay. A review that reports, as must-fix, that the consumer loops or crashes on the invalid frame is a false finding. The final review makes no such must-fix claim.
expectations.evidence: The review has no must-fix findings at all. Its only consumer finding (Medium) is about a malformed HTTP status line (BadStatusLine from getresponse()) escaping the OSError catch in _read_until, not about the consumer looping or crashing on an invalid SSE frame.

expectations.text: [recall:live-endpoint-no-user-agent-silent-exit] The final review reports as must-fix, shown from the code or a local stub (an outside request is not required): The consumer sends no User-Agent header (the live endpoint that the spec names requires one), and every connect failure is swallowed: on an unreachable or refusing endpoint the consumer prints nothing and exits 0.
expectations.evidence: No mention of User-Agent or of connect failures being silently swallowed with exit 0. The review argues the opposite gap (an exception that is NOT swallowed). No must-fix findings exist.

expectations.text: [recall:stop-mid-flush-drops-events] The final review reports as must-fix: A stop or crash between dlt normalize and load leaves a pending package; the next run builds its seen-set and checkpoint without it and drops events it read, against the spec's stop/start rule.
expectations.evidence: No mention of dlt normalize/load, pending packages, seen-set, or checkpoint loss.

expectations.text: [recall:make-stream-fails-on-fresh-tree] The final review reports, at any severity: `make stream` fails on a fresh tree unless `make build` ran first (fact_edit reads lake/sitematrix_sites).
expectations.evidence: The review mentions fact_edit only to say the sitematrix left join cannot fan out; it does not report a make stream / make build ordering failure.

expectations.text: [recall:check-7-test-never-runs-placeholder-row] The final review reports, at any severity: The check-7 dbt test is never selected (no ref()), and when wired in it shows out/marts/late_events holds one all-NULL placeholder row when there are no late events.
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned. The review states the dbt build (26 tests) passed, with no note that a test is unselected or that late_events has a placeholder row.

expectations.text: [recall:dim-date-never-built] The final review reports, at any severity: The date dimension is never built by the build selection, although the spec requires a date dimension.
expectations.evidence: No mention of a date dimension.

expectations.text: [recall:lake-drops-source-fields] The final review reports, at any severity: The lake does not keep the source data: stream_raw drops most event fields and adds derived columns, and the batch lake retypes timestamps and adds variant columns.
expectations.evidence: No mention of the lake dropping or retyping source fields.

expectations.text: [recall:check-4-not-answerable-from-marts] The final review reports, at any severity: Check 4 cannot be answered from out/marts (no state or source totals), and the batch oracle tests go through the same macros as the models.
expectations.evidence: No mention of check 4 or of oracle tests sharing macros with the models; the review instead treats the obligations_per_person macro and the oracle macro as verified correct.

expectations.text: [recall:malformed-event-crashes-on-restart] The final review reports, at any severity: A wrong-typed event (for example a list-valued field) crashes the consumer on every restart, and wrong-typed fields land inconsistent rows.
expectations.evidence: No mention of wrong-typed event fields. The only crash discussed is a malformed HTTP status line.

expectations.text: [recall:territories-published-as-unknown] The final review reports, at any severity: Territories are published with state_name 'UNKNOWN', the same label as the no-state sentinel.
expectations.evidence: No mention of territories or state_name 'UNKNOWN'.

claims_note: The review labels no finding must-fix (it uses Medium and Low only), so the must-fix claims list is empty. Its non-must-fix findings were checked and are recorded under non_must_fix_findings.

non_must_fix_findings.claim: Medium: pipeline/stream_consumer.py _read_until catches only OSError around self._connect(); http.client.HTTPException such as BadStatusLine from getresponse() escapes run() and ends the process.
non_must_fix_findings.evidence: In _read_until the connect is wrapped in 'except OSError: return'. _connect calls conn.request and conn.getresponse unguarded. issubclass(http.client.BadStatusLine, OSError) is False, so it propagates. The connection is also not closed when request()/getresponse() raises, as the review says.

non_must_fix_findings.claim: Low: pipeline/batch_load.py _extract_usaspending takes archive.namelist()[0] as the CSV and uses next(...) with no default for the kind lookup.
non_must_fix_findings.evidence: Lines 29 and 31 of pipeline/batch_load.py match the review's description. These are robustness points, not defects in the given inputs.

suggestions.reason: This control passes trivially for any review with no must-fix findings, including this one, which labels no severity as must-fix. It tests for the absence of a false positive, but it cannot tell a careful review from a shallow one.

The grading prompt asks for must-fix claims, but this reviewer's format (Medium/Low) has no must-fix tier. Defining how to map severities (for example, whether Medium or High counts as must-fix) would make the claims list comparable across configs.

eval_feedback.overall: The review found two minor, real robustness issues and missed every seeded defect. The recall assertions are specific and discriminating.
